facts.raw_span: paroxysmal chest pain
The chest pain had occurred 5 times during the day, and each episode lasted 15 to 30 minutes
blood pressure and pulse rate were 106/52 mm Hg and 64 beats per minutes
normal breath and heart sounds with no murmurs
Hemogram, serum electrolyte levels, kidney and liver function tests, B-type natriuretic peptide and D-dimer levels were all within normal limits
Cardiac troponin I level was 25 ng/mL (normal, <0.023 ng/mL)
sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
sinus bradycardia (46 beats per minute), Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
total occlusion of the right coronary artery (RCA) and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery (LMCA)

concepts.why: The patient's elevated cardiac troponin I level, ST-segment elevation, and Q-wave amplitude deepening on ECG, along with total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery, are indicative of acute myocardial infarction.

The patient's elevated cardiac troponin I level, ST-segment depression, and T-wave inversion on ECG, along with subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery, are indicative of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

The patient's elevated cardiac troponin I level, ST-segment elevation, and Q-wave amplitude deepening on ECG, along with total occlusion of the right coronary artery, are indicative of ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
The patient's paroxysmal chest pain, occurring multiple times during the day, along with subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery, may be indicative of unstable angina.
The patient's total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery are indicative of coronary artery disease.

rationales.F01: Paroxysmal chest pain is a common symptom of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F06: Elevated cardiac troponin I level is a strong indicator of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F07: ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR is indicative of ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: Total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery are indicative of severe coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's ECG findings, including ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, and the elevated cardiac troponin I level, are consistent with ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction, which is a subtype of Acute Myocardial Infarction.
